what_this_is: Paired policy comparison in a labelled simulator. It is not a measurement of any real kitchen.
split: Chronological. Each learner starts empty, predicts before each meal and updates after it. Metrics are computed on the final third of meals only (the test period).
tuning: One policy default (the limit on needing two trips for seconds) was chosen with evaluation/explore_policy.py on development seeds 9001-9002, which are not among the reported seeds. Nothing was chosen using the outputs reported here.
equal_resources: Every policy has the same seconds access, refill size, refill uptake and unlimited stock; kitchen surplus is prepared minus withdrawn under each policy's own preparation rule.

policies.label: Cohort history, same portion for everyone

scenarios.name: baseline
scenarios.description: Mixed appetites, learner's own distribution family.

scenarios.name: gamma_family
scenarios.description: Demand drawn from a gamma family the learner does not assume.

scenarios.name: two_mode_meals
scenarios.description: Each diner has light and heavy meals (bimodal): strong misspecification.

scenarios.name: appetite_rises
scenarios.description: Half the diners' appetite rises 35% a third of the way in.

scenarios.name: late_joiners
scenarios.description: 40% of diners first appear halfway through (cold starts).

scenarios.name: disliked_recipe
scenarios.description: Three meals where the recipe went wrong and half the diners leave food.

scenarios.name: missing_returns
scenarios.description: A quarter of plates never get a return recorded.

scenarios.name: seconds_friction
scenarios.description: Only half of diners who want more walk back for seconds.

scenarios.name: demand_spike
scenarios.description: Three late meals with a jump in attendance and appetite.

limitations: Behaviour (who walks back for seconds, who reports wanting more) follows stated assumptions, not observed diners.
'Left wanting more' uses the simulator's hidden demand, which no real kitchen can observe.
Stock-outs are scored after the fact and do not feed back into what later diners received.
A simulated difference is a property of this simulator. Field effect is unproven until measured in a pilot.
